title: Hilbert's 20th Problem OQ-01: Characterization of Locally Solvable Operators
description: What is the precise characterization of locally solvable operators? Answered by the Nirenberg-Treves conjecture, proved by Dencker (2006): condition (Ψ) on the principal symbol is necessary and sufficient for local solvability of principal-type operators.

meta.author: Nirenberg-Treves (1963), Dencker (2006)
originalContributions: Formalization of linear partial differential operators via multi-index coefficients

overview.historicalContext: Until 1957, it was widely assumed that smooth linear PDEs always have local solutions. Hans Lewy's startling counterexample — a simple first-order operator in ℝ³ with no local solutions — shattered this intuition and launched the modern theory of local solvability. Hörmander (1960) identified the principal symbol as the key invariant and gave a necessary condition: a sign condition involving the Poisson bracket of the real and imaginary parts of the symbol. Nirenberg and Treves (1963) sharpened this to condition (Ψ) — a one-sided sign condition on Im(p_m) along oriented bicharacteristic curves of Re(p_m) — and conjectured it to be both necessary and sufficient for operators of principal type. The necessity half (Hörmander 1960, strengthened by Nirenberg-Treves 1963) was established relatively quickly. The sufficiency direction resisted all attempts for 43 years: partial results by Beals-Fefferman (1973, condition (P), a stronger condition), and Lerner (1988-2000, partial cases) fell short of condition (Ψ). Dencker's 2006 proof of sufficiency — using sophisticated second microlocalization and energy estimates — completed the conjecture and earned the Bôcher Memorial Prize.
overview.problemStatement: What is the precise characterization of locally solvable operators? That is, given a linear partial differential operator P, when does the equation Pu = f have a distribution solution u near a point x₀ for every smooth f?
overview.text: We formalize the answer: for operators of principal type, local solvability is equivalent to condition (Ψ) on the principal symbol.
overview.proofStrategy: Define linear PDOs, principal symbols, local solvability, principal type, and condition (Ψ). State the Hörmander necessity and Dencker sufficiency as axioms, then derive the characterization. Show elliptic operators as a key special case.
keyInsights: The principal symbol p_m(x, ξ) encodes the leading-order behavior of the operator: it isolates the degree-m part, replacing ∂/∂xᵢ with the dual variable ξᵢ. All classical PDE properties (ellipticity, hyperbolicity, local solvability) are determined by p_m, not the lower-order terms.

Condition (Ψ): Im(p_m) cannot change sign from − to + along oriented bicharacteristic curves of Re(p_m). The asymmetry is key: − to + transitions are forbidden, but + to − transitions are allowed. This directional sign condition captures exactly the obstruction found in Lewy's 1957 example.

Elliptic operators satisfy (Ψ) vacuously: since p_m(x, ξ) ≠ 0 for all ξ ≠ 0, no bicharacteristic curves exist (they require p_m = 0 along the curve), so the universal quantifier in (Ψ) has empty domain and is trivially true.

The Nirenberg-Treves conjecture took 43 years to prove (1963-2006). The necessity half was established by Hörmander (1960). Sufficiency resisted all attempts — Beals-Fefferman (1973) proved the stronger condition (P) sufficient, Lerner made partial progress — until Dencker's 2006 breakthrough using second microlocalization and energy estimates.

Encoding BicharacteristicCurve as a concrete structure (not an axiom) enables Lean to construct concrete objects and reason about them in proved theorems. The omission of the Hamilton flow ODE condition makes the definition more general than the classical one — more curves to check — which strengthens (Ψ) conservatively, so the axioms remain sound.

The three axioms are architecturally distinct: `IsLocallySolvable` is a foundational gap (distributions not in Mathlib), while `hormander_necessity` and `dencker_sufficiency` are mathematical gaps (deep microlocal analysis awaiting Lean formalization). This hierarchy tells us what to build first.

sections.title: Module Header and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring gives historical table (Lewy 1957 through Dencker 2006), states condition (Ψ), documents the 3 remaining axioms, and notes the bicharacteristic concretization. Imports Mathlib inner product spaces, normed fields, metric spaces, and FDeriv. Opens namespace `Hilbert20LocalSolvability`.

sections.title: Part I: Linear Differential Operators
sections.summary: Defines `MultiIndex n` (= Fin n → ℕ), `MultiIndex.order` (sum of exponents), `LinearPDO n m` (structure storing smooth coefficient functions a_α : ℝⁿ → ℂ indexed by multi-indices with order ≤ m), and `principalSymbol` (the degree-m part: p_m(x,ξ) = Σ_{|α|=m} a_α(x) ξ^α).

sections.title: Part II: Local Solvability
sections.summary: Axiomatizes `IsLocallySolvable P x₀ : Prop` (distributions not in Mathlib). Defines `IsPrincipalType P`: the symbol gradient ∇_ξ p_m is nonzero wherever p_m vanishes for ξ ≠ 0, ensuring non-degeneracy of the bicharacteristic flow direction.

sections.title: Part III: Condition (Ψ) and Bicharacteristics
sections.summary: Defines `BicharacteristicCurve P` as a concrete structure (x(t), ξ(t) with symbol vanishing and ξ ≠ 0; Hamilton flow omitted). Defines `imSymbolAlongCurve γ t = Im(p_m(γ(t)))`. Proves bridge lemma `imSymbolAlongCurve_eq`. Defines `ConditionPsi P`: Im(p_m) cannot go from negative to positive along any bicharacteristic curve.

sections.title: Part IV: The Nirenberg-Treves Theorem
sections.summary: Axiomatizes `hormander_necessity` (condition (Ψ) is necessary, Hörmander 1960) and `dencker_sufficiency` (condition (Ψ) is sufficient, Dencker 2006). Proves `nirenberg_treves_characterization`: `IsLocallySolvable P x₀ ↔ ConditionPsi P` via `Iff.intro`.

sections.title: Part V: Important Special Cases
sections.summary: Proves `real_symbol_satisfies_psi` (if Im p_m = 0 everywhere, (Ψ) holds vacuously). Defines `IsElliptic`. Proves `elliptic_satisfies_psi` (no bicharacteristic curves exist for elliptic P, via `absurd`). Derives `elliptic_locally_solvable` combining both.

conclusion.summary: We formalize the answer to Hilbert's 20th problem OQ-01: the Nirenberg-Treves conjecture (proved by Dencker, 2006) gives the precise characterization of locally solvable operators. For principal-type operators, local solvability is equivalent to condition (Ψ) on the principal symbol. Two special cases are fully proved in Lean: elliptic operators (vacuously, no bicharacteristics exist) and real-symbol operators (Im p_m = 0 forbids any negative starting point).
conclusion.implications:
**Mathematical significance of the Nirenberg-Treves characterization:**

1. **RESOLUTION OF A 43-YEAR PROBLEM**: The Nirenberg-Treves conjecture (1963-2006) was one of the most celebrated open problems in PDE theory. Dencker's proof completed the characterization: for principal-type operators, condition (Ψ) is the *only* obstruction to local solvability. This formalization captures the logical skeleton of the equivalence — the iff structure — while naming the two hard analytic halves as axioms awaiting future formalization.

2. **THE LEWY EXAMPLE IN CONTEXT**: Hans Lewy's 1957 counterexample has principal symbol $p = \xi_1 + iz\xi_3$, and $\mathrm{Im}(p)$ changes sign along bicharacteristics of $\mathrm{Re}(p)$, violating condition (Ψ). Dencker's theorem explains *why* Lewy's operator is non-solvable. The formalization could in principle construct the Lewy operator as a `LinearPDO` and verify that it fails `ConditionPsi`.

3. **SYMPLECTIC GEOMETRY AS THE HIDDEN STRUCTURE**: The bicharacteristic curves are Hamilton flow lines of $H = \mathrm{Re}(p_m)$ on the symplectic manifold $T^*\mathbb{R}^n$. The sign condition in (Ψ) is precisely the condition that prevents $\mathrm{Im}(p_m)$ from acting as a source of energy along the cotangent bundle flow — this is the geometric content of Dencker's energy estimates.

4. **THE AXIOM ARCHITECTURE AS A ROADMAP**: `IsLocallySolvable` is a *foundational gap* (once Mathlib has Schwartz distributions, this can be concretely defined). `hormander_necessity` and `dencker_sufficiency` are *mathematical gaps* (require pseudodifferential operator calculus, $L^2$ Carleman estimates, second microlocalization). This hierarchy tells us what to build first.

5. **ELLIPTIC REGULARITY BY A NEW PATH**: `elliptic_locally_solvable` is an independent proof of local solvability for elliptic operators via the purely algebraic route: elliptic ⟹ no bicharacteristics ⟹ (Ψ) vacuously ⟹ solvable. This makes the elliptic case rigorous without any function space machinery beyond the axioms.
openQuestions: Once Mathlib acquires Schwartz distribution theory, can `IsLocallySolvable` be replaced by a concrete definition? The key ingredient is the topological dual of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ — Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap` framework may eventually provide this.

The `BicharacteristicCurve` structure omits the Hamilton flow ODE condition pending Mathlib ODE infrastructure. Once available, can the structure be strengthened to the classical definition, and do the proved theorems lift automatically?

The analogue of condition (Ψ) for *systems* of PDEs (where the principal symbol is a matrix) remains an open problem. Can this matrix version be formalized using Mathlib's `Matrix` and spectral theory?
Can Lewy's 1957 example be constructed as a specific `LinearPDO` that is verified to fail `ConditionPsi`, providing a concrete computational witness to the necessity direction?

crossReferences.description: Parent entry — Hilbert's 20th problem on boundary value problems for PDEs. This OQ-01 specializes to the local solvability question, the most surprising aspect given Lewy's 1957 counterexample.
The Navier-Stokes formalization also faces the foundational gap: Schwartz distributions are not yet in Mathlib, requiring axiomatization of key analytic properties in both entries.

The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality underlies the $L^2$ energy estimates in Dencker's proof of sufficiency. The `InnerProductSpace` Mathlib module used here provides the functional analytic foundation on which microlocal energy estimates would be built.
